title: Money and Everyday Arithmetic
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Money and Everyday Arithmetic. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Everyday calculations

Keep money values in one currency and align decimal places when adding or subtracting. A budget compares income with expenses; balance is income minus spending. For repeated purchases, multiply the price per item by the quantity.

Unit price and sale price

Unit price is (\(total price/quantity\)). Discount amount is (discount rate times marked price), and sale price is (\(marked price \times (1-discount rate)\)). Tax is calculated using the base specified by the problem; add it after discount only when the stated rules say so.

Interest and installments

Simple interest is (\(I=Prt\)) when rate is expressed as a decimal and time units match the rate period. Total repayment is principal plus interest; any installment calculation must also consider the number and timing of payments if specified.

Worked example: An item marked Rs 2,000 has a 15% discount. Discount is (\(0.15 \times 2000=Rs 300\)); sale price before any separately stated tax is Rs 1,700.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Compare unit prices only after converting quantities to the same unit.
  • Calculate percentage discount from the marked price unless another base is stated.
  • Keep discount, tax and final payment as separate steps.
  • Estimate a total before exact calculation to catch misplaced decimals.
  • For simple interest, convert months to years when the annual rate is used.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Sale price = marked price - discount.
  • Simple interest: (\(I=Prt\)); amount: (\(A=P+I\)).
  • A percentage is a rate per 100; 18% = 0.18.
  • Round currency to the smallest permitted unit only at the final step.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A customer pays ₹500 for a bill of ₹376. What change is due?

    1. ₹114
    2. ₹124
    3. ₹134
    4. ₹224
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: ₹124

    Change (\(=500-376=₹124\)).

  2. Core:

    An ₹800 item has a 10% discount. What is the price after discount?

    1. ₹700
    2. ₹710
    3. ₹720
    4. ₹780
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: ₹720

    Discount (\(=0.10\cdot800=₹80\)). Price (\(=800-80=₹720\)).

  3. Foundation:

    A customer buys items costing Rs 38.50 and Rs 24.75 and pays Rs 100. How much change is due?

    1. (\(Rs 26.25\))
    2. (\(Rs 36.75\))
    3. (\(Rs 37.25\))
    4. (\(Rs 38.75\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(Rs 36.75\))

    Total is (\(38.50+24.75=Rs 63.25\)). Change is (\(100-63.25=Rs 36.75\)).

  4. Standard:

    A Rs 1,500 item is discounted by 20%. Find its sale price before tax.

    1. (\(Rs 1,100\))
    2. (\(Rs 1,200\))
    3. (\(Rs 1,250\))
    4. (\(Rs 1,300\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(Rs 1,200\))

    Discount is (\(0.20 \times 1500=Rs 300\)). Sale price is (\(1500-300=Rs 1,200\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Find simple interest on Rs 8,000 at 7.5% per year for 2 years.

    1. (\(Rs 600\))
    2. (\(Rs 1,000\))
    3. (\(Rs 1,200\))
    4. (\(Rs 1,500\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(Rs 1,200\))

    (\(I=Prt=8000 \times 0.075 \times 2=Rs 1,200\)).
